reasons: Reproduced: variant compiles; testForID_String fails with expected:<-07:05:34[]> but was:<-07:05:34[.000]>; full suite (3828 tests) fails only the trigger; correct.patch gives 0 failures. (a) Only the gold computes the zone id, and it alone turns correct input (offset -25534000, verified via hop 4's parseOffset) into a wrong value: its javadoc promises 'the timezone offset string of the offset' as the id, and the codebase's timezone offset string for this offset (DateTimeZone.printOffset, 'Formats a timezone offset string', used by forOffsetMillis/forTimeZone) is -07:05:34; the variant makes forID("-07:05:34.0") unequal to forOffsetMillis of the same offset. Hops 1-4 and the facade only fail transitively. (b) Each hop's javadoc matches its code (UTC check; provider lookup; +/- acceptance else IAE; parse + zero->UTC); none mentions or forms the id, and hop 4 hands over the offset only, so no hop doc admits the observed id. (c) The gold's id depends only on the int offset and, with the fault, any offset with a sub-minute part yields hh:mm:ss.mmm, so no change of the id or offset above the gold can produce -07:05:34 (hop-3 normalisation and hop-4 rounding both fail). The only passing edits discard or override the gold's output (hop 4 -> forOffsetMillis; hop 4 post-editing the gold's id; fixedOffsetZone ignoring its id): bypasses. (d) Hop/gold names are neutral (zoneForId, zoneFromId, zoneOfId, zoneForOffsetId, zoneForOffset), no added comments in the gold, G2b clean; the lie ('Region IDs are looked up by a binary search in a sorted array of all the available IDs') is false (ConcurrentHashMap lookup) and names neither the fault nor the omitted step. (e) Gold is 5 calls below forID; hosts are 5 distinct existing classes (PeriodFormatterBuilder, DateTimeZoneBuilder, ISODateTimeFormat, DateTime, Period); facade = null guard + one delegating call; one added procedural sentence; gold javadoc silent on omitting a zero millisecond rest; trigger is an existing test, empty test.patch, sole new failure. (f) Pinned outside the gold by DateTimeZone.printOffset (returns after seconds when rest==0) and DateTimeFormatterBuilder.TimeZoneOffset.printTo (returns after seconds when the rest is zero), and by passing tests testForOffsetMillis_int / testForOffsetHoursMinutes_int_int / testForTimeZone_TimeZone (forID ids equal printOffset-built ids; zero rests omitted).
notes: Bypass edits recorded above. No passing test pins exactly the 'seconds present, zero millis' case other than the trigger; the pin for that case is code (printOffset, TimeZoneOffset.printTo). The lie is placed after the @throws tag with irregular indentation (no leading '*'), so in rendered javadoc it reads as part of the @throws text; it is still one added sentence in the facade javadoc. The @FromString annotation was moved onto the return type (behaviour-preserving). parseOffset and fixedOffsetZone were widened from private to package-private to make the chain compile. The only shape cue in the gold is that the seconds group is guarded by rest != 0 while the millisecond tail is not; this was not assessed against the no-local-trace checklist (out of scope for this audit). Note for re-runs: copying a compiled workspace and editing within the same second leaves stale classes; trials were run with build/ removed.
